title: Refactor routing dispatcher for regional affinity, tiered routing, and graceful model-variant fallbacks
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Refactor the routing dispatcher component to natively understand regional affinity, customer tier routing, and a prioritized fallback chain of model variants. The goal is to simplify policy config surface for product teams, reduce misroutes under capacity pressure, and make safe, observable rollouts for variant-based fallbacks.
background: Current routing behavior is a mix of hard-coded heuristics and a brittle policy interpreter. We've seen three recurring issues: 1) requests routed cross-region causing added latency for region-sensitive customers; 2) tiered customers being routed to incompatible model variants during failover; 3) complex config changes causing silent misroutes during canaries. This ticket consolidates the dispatcher logic and introduces an explicit routing graph with affinity scoring and deterministic fallback sequencing.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Routing Dispatcher that consumes normalized route graphs produced by the existing policy compiler. Key capabilities: regional affinity tags on routes, tier-aware matchers (e.g., premium, standard, free), explicit fallback chains with weighted priorities, and a sandboxed evaluation mode for dry-run canaries. The dispatcher will expose tracing spans and metrics for every decision point to the Console for troubleshooting.
migration_plan: 1) Add dispatcher interface and opt-in feature flag. 2) Run shadow mode for 2 weeks where decisions are logged but not enforced. 3) Enable canary enforcement for a small percentage of traffic on non-critical customers. 4) Gradual ramp while monitoring key metrics and test prompt sets. 5) Full cutover and deprecation of legacy heuristics.
rollout_strategy: Shadow -> Canary (1%, 5%, 25%) -> Ramp (50%) -> Full. Use customer label targeting to exclude high-SLA enterprise orgs until confidence thresholds are met. Automated rollback if latency or error-rate SLOs degrade beyond thresholds.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after incidents where cross-region routing increased P95 by 120ms.
2026-03-11: Spike completed — benchmarked naive dispatcher loop; identified KV cache key impacts; estimated ~2-4% request-side CPU overhead for improved decision traces.
2026-03-12: Implemented dispatcher interface and added feature-flag gate; pushed initial PR for skeleton (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287).
2026-03-13: Integrated trace spans for routing decisions into trace context; started a small shadow run against beta cluster.
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): prefer explicit prioritization semantics in config so product teams can reason about fallback order.
Design (Rosa Kim): surface per-route latency and cost estimate in Console when choosing fallback variants.
SRE (Marcus Diaz): gate rollout behind autoscaler config to avoid capacity blowouts during canaries.
Security (Anika Sharma): ensure the dispatcher does not add new privileges; security review scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher evaluates routing graph and produces deterministic route decisions for same inputs 100% of the time.
Shadow logs match legacy decision rates within a 0.5% delta before enforcement.
Canary enforcement passes for 3 consecutive days without latency or error regression beyond alert thresholds.
Telemetry: per-decision trace span, routing_reason tag, and a percent-matched metric emitted to Console.
Config: new route attributes (region_affinity, tier_match, fallback_chain) documented and validated by CI linter.
risks: Incorrect fallback sequencing could cause customer requests to hit incompatible quantized variants and regress quality.
Increased dispatcher latency could affect tail latency; need microbenchmarks and fast-path for simple rules.
Config migration may introduce silent misroutes if older policies are not normalized — include a migration verifier.
qa_plan: Create unit tests for rule permutations, simulating region down events, tier overrides, and variant failures. Add e2e tests using production-like traffic sampler and a test harness that injects artificial model failures. Run shadow comparison daily and assert decision parity metrics.
notes: We deliberately avoid introducing a new DSL in this ticket; dispatcher consumes normalized graph output from the policy compiler to keep responsibilities separated.
Follow-on work will include Console UX for editing fallback chains and a linter to prevent contradictory rules.
